objective: Freeze HTTP/2 receive credit and bounded-buffer accounting around the actual h2 flow-control boundary.

decision.expected: WINDOW_UPDATE and peer DATA progress follow released bytes only.
decision.production_release: ReceiveBody reports previous DATA length on its next poll, releases accumulated bytes via h2::FlowControl::release_capacity, flushes partial credit when h2 returns Pending, and releases/removes its slot at terminal completion or Drop.
decision.public_boundary: BrowserConnection/BrowserChannel/ReceiveBody are the production browser receive path; NativeAdmission/TunnelStream are the native measured transport. ReceiveCredit is crate-private and the browser body is wasm-only.

bounds.observation_limit: ConnectionSnapshot counts actual DATA and connection WINDOW_UPDATE frames plus Rust callback/pipe capacities; it excludes allocator metadata, h2 buffers and browser engine allocations before callbacks.

integration_test.boundary: Uses actual h2 client/server SendStream and RecvStream over bounded Tokio async I/O. Four stream windows remain owned without capacity release until the aggregate receive window stalls; releasing bytes must wake the blocked peer sender and return DATA.
assertions: Polling and retaining four stream windows leaves used_capacity unchanged and exhausts the actual shared connection window.
The next DATA byte remains blocked until the consumer releases a held DATA buffer.
Releasing held DATA restores h2 send capacity and the corresponding DATA is observed by the receiver.
After terminal bodies are drained, used_capacity is zero while body values remain retained.
limits: This host integration target exercises h2 flow-control windows directly; it does not import private ReceiveCredit or claim its slot bookkeeping is covered here.
Existing resources.rs real-h2 unit tests cover ReceiveCredit partial batches, aggregate credit, slot reuse, failed release visibility and slot ownership.
The actual df-tools browser connection-credit fixture is still required to exercise BrowserConnection/BrowserChannel/ReceiveBody in wasm.

test_fixture_window_settings.reason: The host contract deliberately raises each test stream window to the production connection-window size so four streams exhaust shared connection credit before any one stream exhausts its own window.

task_ownership.server_owner: The server task retains every producer JoinHandle, receives an explicit stop signal after terminal bodies drain, and awaits all producers before returning.
task_ownership.client_owner: The client driver is explicitly aborted and its JoinHandle is awaited; unexpected driver errors remain failures.
task_ownership.producer_errors: Producer h2 send errors and producer task panics propagate through explicit expectations and JoinHandle awaits.

integration_test.terminal_accounting: Each producer sends an explicit empty END_STREAM DATA frame. The receiver checks any terminal frame has no payload, confirms end-of-stream, checks subsequent data() returns None, and retains completed bodies with zero used_capacity.

browser_fixture.scenario: Run the current four-stream held/resumed connection-credit fixture at the pinned candidate build; retain its explicit INCONCLUSIVE branch when snapshots do not establish exhausted connection DATA credit and stalled DATA/WINDOW_UPDATE progress.
evidence_requirements: Four stream results with held and resumed measurements.
